issues.body: The record still requires the groom lane to resolve a stale differing-value maximum-generation tie by applying the deterministic tie-break, while the exhaustive delete rule permits a maximum-generation deletion only for the deleter's own record when a smaller sibling is present. A later groom owns neither dead writer's operation record. No promotion or delegated-delete transition is defined, so the required sweep remains forbidden by the protocol and the disarm latch may remain UNKNOWN indefinitely.
issues.fix_hint: Define a concrete fenced transition the groom is authorized to perform, including concurrency semantics and non-vacuous interleaving tests. For example, specify deterministic promotion of the selected value at a fresh generation, or narrowly authorize and authenticate groom deletion of the selected loser while preserving the never-delete-winner invariant.
issues.title: The stale-tie groom still cannot delete a dead writer's loser

issues.body: Step 0 still says that finding a record carrying `(N, op)` means the operation landed and immediately returns it. It does not fetch or compare the record body with the expected operation body under the declared volatile-field equivalence rule. Thus corruption, an operation-digest collision, or a divergent writer at the same path is silently accepted on retry instead of producing conflict/UNKNOWN. The later requirement to test varying bodies against the store does not cover this early-return bypass.
issues.fix_hint: Require step 0 rediscovery to read and validate the existing record using the declared equivalence rule before returning. Divergence must fail closed. Add a restart/lost-response test with a matching `(N, op)` filename but non-equivalent bytes and assert conflict or UNKNOWN rather than success.
issues.title: Step 0 still accepts a matching path without validating its body

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Round 5 leaves both round-4 soundness gaps materially unchanged. The stale differing-value tie is still assigned to a groom that is not authorized by the stated delete invariant to remove either dead writer's maximum-generation loser, so UNKNOWN can remain permanent. Step 0 still returns solely on an `(N, op)` filename match without fetching and validating the immutable body, bypassing the record's own create-or-keep equivalence rule. The added implementation-test requirement for attempt-varying bodies does not repair that protocol path. Both are load-bearing correctness defects, so changes remain required.
